elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED..." — the cap runs to each party, not only the counterparty.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap reads only "THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY SANOFI UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE CLAIM"; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. To reach preferred, insert "THE GREATER OF (A) ... AND (B) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained first sentence: "NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, PUNITIVE, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES OR LOST PROFITS..."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Retained: "NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 ... SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT ... DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO CONFIDENTIALITY UNDER ARTICLE XI"; the new cap sentence sits in Section 14.5 and is further prefaced "EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN THE PRECEDING SENTENCE".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list covers only indemnification (14.1/14.2), confidentiality (Article XI) and intellectual property (Article X); no data protection or security obligations are named, and the new cap therefore captures them.

Retained: "NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 IS INTENDED TO OR SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE INDEMNIFICATION RIGHTS OR OBLIGATIONS OF ANY PARTY UNDER SECTION 14.1 OR SECTION 14.2"; the cap is expressly subject to that sentence.
New sentence opens "EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN THE PRECEDING SENTENCE AND WITH RESPECT TO A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT".
Same express exception: "WITH RESPECT TO A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT".
Fraud appears nowhere in the carve-out language of Section 14.5 as rendered; add "FRAUD" to the exception list to reach preferred.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The retained carve-out preserves "DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO ... INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY UNDER ARTICLE X". Whether Article X obligations extend to infringement of the other party's IP (as opposed to licence/ownership covenants) cannot be determined from the excerpt supplied.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No sentence states that Sanofi's payment obligations (e.g., the Section 9.2 milestone payments) are not "damages" subject to the cap; as drafted the cap literally reaches liability for unpaid amounts.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED..." — symmetrical in party direction.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY SANOFI UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — a 12-month fee-based measure, matching the fallback basis.

Cap is prefaced "EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN THE PRECEDING SENTENCE", which preserves indemnification under Sections 14.1/14.2 without limitation, and that sentence independently disapplies anything "IN THIS SECTION 14.5".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Article XI confidentiality damages remain unrestricted by "anything in this Section 14.5", which now includes the new cap sentence.
Express exception for "A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE" in the cap sentence.
Express exception for "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" in the cap sentence.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted sentence supplies a mutual aggregate cap measured by 12 months of fees, and the four required carve-outs (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct) all sit outside it — two via the retained "nothing in this Section 14.5" sentence and two by express words in the new sentence. The 'EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN THE PRECEDING SENTENCE' anchor is unambiguous because the new sentence immediately follows the carve-out sentence.

Preferred level is not reached on four points the drafter must add if pressed: (i) the "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor is absent; (ii) data protection and security obligations are not carved out; (iii) fraud is not carved out; (iv) there is no statement that Customer payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. IP infringement is only partially addressed via the Article X reference and cannot be confirmed from the excerpt.

Minimality holds: a single sentence is inserted, nothing is deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category is added, and the gross negligence / willful misconduct words are required by the chosen fallback checklist rather than being extras.
Intent preserved: the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the 14.1/14.2 indemnity carve-out and the Article X/XI carve-outs all survive unchanged, and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting caution (not a defect against the checklist): this is a collaboration/licence structure whose consideration is upfront, milestone ($520,000,000 under Section 9.2) and royalty payments, and lowercase "fees" is not a defined term here. Consider anchoring the cap to "all amounts paid or payable by Sanofi under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months..." or adding a payment-obligations carve-out so the cap is neither illusory nor read as limiting Sanofi's Section 9.2 payment liability.
